knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A tripping safety switch is a fault signal. Resetting it to keep working can hide the fault and create a shock risk.
A missing earth pin and a damaged cord fail the pre-use check. The item is tagged and removed from service.
Near electrical parts a damp cloth is used rather than spray, to keep water away from live parts.
Water at a damaged lead is a stop sign. The worker keeps clear, isolates if safe, records and refers.
Repair of fixed wiring and switchboards is regulated electrical work that needs a licence holder. The course does not grant that licence.

practicalCriteria: Completes a pre-use check of each powered item before it is used
Tests the site RCD by the site procedure before using water on the job
Keeps water and product away from sockets, switches, terminals and motor vents
Stops and refers on any stop-and-refer sign, and does not reset a tripped switch
passRule: Knowledge checks: at least 4 of 5 correct (80%). Practical sign-off is separate: an assessor observes the practical criteria and records the result. A knowledge pass is not practical competence and does not grant any licence or authority.
evidenceRequired: Pre-use check record for each powered item
RCD test result from the site procedure
Fault record and referral for any stop-and-refer event
stopWorkCriteria: A safety switch trips and the worker resets it to continue
Water found inside a control housing or at a damaged lead
Any heat, smell, sparks or exposed conductor
